_note: This is the chart used throughout the Life Blueprint project this engine grew out of. It is a REAL, already-computed reference (originally generated by Prokerala.com), not a synthetic test case. Personal details beyond birth data are intentionally omitted here -- this fixture exists purely for engine validation, not as a stored user record.
_status: MOSTLY VERIFIED against real @swisseph/browser output, via both a raw-ephemeris check (tests/golden-charts/ephemeris.test.ts) and the full computeChart() pipeline (tests/golden-charts/full-chart.test.ts) -- see DECISIONS.md, last updated 2026-07-28. All 9 planet longitudes and the Ascendant were computed and compared. Within the stated 1 arc-minute tolerance: Moon (0.79'), Mercury (0.57'), Venus (0.31'), Jupiter (0.50'), Saturn (0.85'), and the Ascendant (0.40'). Just outside the 1' tolerance: Sun (1.20'), Mars (1.25'), Rahu and Ketu (1.03' each) -- CORRECTED 2026-07-28: an earlier version of this note incorrectly filed Rahu/Ketu under 'within tolerance' (1.03' > 1.00' tolerance, a plain arithmetic slip); caught when full-chart.test.ts checked every planet without an early-exit, where the previous, narrower test had thrown on Sun before ever reaching Rahu. DECISION: left failing on purpose, not tightened or loosened -- see DECISIONS.md for the full reasoning. In short: all 9 bodies ran through the identical calculatePosition() code path with identical flags, and Mercury -- in the same 9th-house cluster as Sun and Mars in this chart, so not a fluke of a shared calculation branch -- passed clean at 0.57'. There's no mechanism specific to these four bodies in the pipeline; the pattern points to imprecision in this fixture's own hand/spreadsheet-derived values, not a code defect. It's also not a correctness risk to the engine as built: sub-1.3-arcminute deltas this small don't cross any sign, house, or nakshatra boundary the engine actually reasons about (nakshatra spans are 13d20', house/sign boundaries are 30d) -- this is fixture-confidence noise, not a blocking bug. Proper resolution deferred to a second, independent golden chart once the golden-chart set expands past this single fixture (see BACKLOG.md) -- cross-referencing against an independent source is the right way to settle whether this fixture or the ephemeris is closer to true, not further tightening ephemeris precision. Jupiter's dignity was corrected from the original source's 'neutral' to 'friend' -- see the `_correctedFrom` note on that field and DECISIONS.md; Scorpio's lord is Mars, and Jupiter/Mars are natural friends per BPHS, not neutral. FULLY SWEPT 2026-07-28 (every hand-derived value in this fixture checked against real ephemeris/pipeline output, not just the ones that happened to come up first): ascendant.nakshatra, Moon.nakshatra/nakshatraPada, navamsaD9 (Ascendant + all 9 planet D9 signs), dashaBalanceAtBirth, and mahadashaSequence are now all verified in full-chart.test.ts -- all match, EXCEPT mahadashaSequence's exact dates, which are a consistent ~3 days off across all 9 boundaries (see full-chart.test.ts's own comment: this is the expected, predicted-in-advance-by-SKILL.md's-own-dasha.md consequence of the Moon-longitude gap already documented above, not a new bug -- a constant, non-growing offset is the signature of that, not of a chaining bug). Along the way this also caught and fixed a real bug in dasha.ts: computeMahadashaSequence() was anchoring the birth Mahadasha's `start` at the birth instant instead of its true (pre-birth) start, which also silently corrupted that Mahadasha's own Antardasha proportions -- see DECISIONS.md. yogasExpected is checked (the 6 yogas/doshas this project implements; RajaYoga_9th is out of scope, not a gap). Only field never independently checked against anything beyond internal consistency: `expectedSettings` (ayanamsa/nodeType/houseSystem) -- these are configuration echoed back, not computed astrological facts, so 'verification' doesn't apply the same way; they're asserted to match DEFAULT_ENGINE_SETTINGS structurally via TypeScript, not spot-checked here. Also note: this file's `yogasExpected` object had a JSON syntax error (closed with `]` instead of `}`) that made the entire file unparseable JSON until fixed 2026-07-28 -- see DECISIONS.md. CORRECTED 2026-08-07: the sentence above blaming the Sun/Mars/Rahu/Ketu and mahadashaSequence gaps on 'imprecision in this fixture's own hand/spreadsheet-derived values' was itself wrong -- the raw Prokerala source (tests/golden-charts/sources/reference-chart-1983-prokerala-raw.md, now checked into the repo) was located and every one of this file's hand-transcribed values (all 9 planet degrees, all 9 Mahadasha dates, plus all 81 Antardasha and 729 Pratyantardasha boundaries -- see reference-chart-1983-dasha-detail.json) was independently re-verified against it and found to match EXACTLY. The gap is real and is NOT this fixture's own transcription error -- it's a genuine Prokerala-vs-this-project's-own-engine (Moshier-based) difference. The 'second, independent golden chart' resolution path in BACKLOG.md is still open and still the right next step (this pass verified the FIRST source more thoroughly, it did not add a second one) -- see DECISIONS.md, 2026-08-07.
